Triggers.value: A memory of the event coming to mind suddenly

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Places of worship or religious gatherings

Threat.value: Being superalert or watchful or on guard
Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard
I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger

Memory.value: I cannot tell a clear story of what happened even to myself
Some moments of the event are extremely clear while others are completely blank
When I try to explain what happened I lose the thread and cannot finish

Negative Appraisals.value: I acted in ways that go against who I am
I am not sure my life is worth living anymore

vignette: Sophia, a 39-year-old Oceania woman and park ranger in Hawaii, has recently returned from serving as a relief worker in a war-torn region. Her experience there has left her grappling with a complex array of symptoms that have significantly impacted her daily life and relationships. One morning while on patrol at the national park, Sophia was suddenly overwhelmed by an intrusive memory of the traumatic event she had witnessed. The scent of perfume worn by a colleague triggered vivid recollections of the war zone, and the sight of two visitors sharing a tender hug further intensified the flashback. These triggers have become increasingly potent over time, leading her to develop maladaptive strategies such as avoiding medical care or religious spaces where she might encounter similar scents or displays of affection. Sophia has come to believe that her life is no longer worth living and that she no longer belongs anywhere. These negative appraisals have reinforced her hypervigilance, making her constantly on guard for any sudden movements by others. This heightened state of alertness has also contributed to her avoidance of unfamiliar places, as she fears being unable to assess potential dangers adequately. Her memory of the traumatic event is fragmented and incoherent. Some moments are crystal clear, while others remain entirely blank, leaving her unable to construct a coherent narrative even for herself. When Sophia tries to explain what happened, she often loses track of her thoughts and cannot complete her story. This disintegration of memory has exacerbated her feelings of being violated by actions that go against her core values, leading to further avoidance behaviors. The interplay between these factors has created a self-reinforcing cycle where Sophia's triggers activate her negative appraisals, which in turn lead to maladaptive strategies and heightened threat perceptions. For example, whenever she smells perfume or sees people expressing affection, she immediately feels that her life is not worth living and becomes hypervigilant, avoiding places and situations that might retrigger these memories. Sophia's occupation as a park ranger has also been affected by this cycle. Her hypervigilance towards sudden movements and unfamiliar places has made it difficult for her to perform routine tasks, leading to an increase in anxiety and avoidance behaviors. She has come to believe that she no longer fits into the role of a park ranger and feels out of place even among colleagues who show affection or use perfumes. Sophia's marriage has also suffered due to these symptoms. Her husband often finds her distant and preoccupied, as she struggles with intrusive memories and negative appraisals that keep her on edge. The avoidance behaviors have created significant tension between them, as Sophia pulls away from physical affection and social gatherings, further reinforcing her sense of isolation. What finally brought Sophia to seek help was a particularly severe episode triggered by a familiar perfume scent at a family gathering. This incident left her feeling overwhelmed and unable to function normally, leading her to realize that the cycle she was caught in could no longer be ignored. She is most afraid of losing control completely but hopes for a way to regain some sense of normalcy and connection with those around her. In summary, Sophia's experience illustrates how triggers, maladaptive strategies, threat perceptions, memory fragmentation, and negative appraisals can form a complex and self-reinforcing cycle that significantly impacts daily functioning and relationships. Her journey towards recovery will involve addressing these interconnected elements to break the reinforcing loop and find ways to manage her symptoms effectively.
